additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is defined by recurrent episodes of consuming an unusually large amount of food in a discrete period while experiencing a loss of control, accompanied by features such as rapid eating, eating until uncomfortably full, and marked guilt or disgust afterward. It commonly develops or becomes recognized during periods of stress, isolation, disrupted routine, or shame around eating, and is distinguished from bulimia nervosa by the absence of regular compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise.

patient.stressor: Maria lost a close friend from her walking club and church choir, someone who had shared weekly Mass, crochet projects, and quiet conversations about family history. In the three months that followed, the empty afternoons after choir practice and gardening became times when she would prepare familiar Puerto Rican foods for comfort and sometimes eat much larger amounts than she intended, more quickly than her usual slow meals, until she felt overly full. The episodes were not constant, but the sense of not being able to stop once she began and the guilt afterward troubled her because food had always represented care, tradition, and family connection rather than secrecy. She brought it up herself during a routine primary-care visit, and her doctor arranged a psychiatric consultation after recognizing that the pattern had persisted for several months.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: Some afternoons after choir or working in the garden, I fix myself a plate of rice and beans or chicken stew, and then I keep going back for more until I’ve eaten enough for two or three meals.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: What brings me in is that once I start eating those comfort foods, I tell myself, 'Maria, that is enough,' but my hand still goes back to the pot like I can’t make myself stop.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I have always been a slow eater, but lately when this happens I eat fast standing by the counter, hardly tasting the food before the next bite is already in my mouth.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: By the time I stop, my stomach feels tight and heavy, and I have to sit in my recliner with my waistband loosened because I went past what felt comfortable.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: Afterward I feel ashamed and sad, like I turned something that used to mean family and caring into something I have to hide from people at church.

add_requirements.binge_eating_at_least_once_weekly_for_3_: Since my friend passed, this has been happening most weeks, usually once or twice in those quiet afternoons after choir or gardening.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I still go to Mass, choir, and take care of my home, but after one of these afternoons I may stay in and avoid calling anyone because I feel embarrassed.
add_requirements.duration: This started after my close friend died, and it has been going on for about three months now.
